class.name: SubWorld
class.brief_description: Constrains child nodes to a specific [World3D] other than what is used by its [Viewport].
class.description:
A [SubWorld] contrains its children to a specific [World3D] and creates a disconnect from any given [Viewport]. Originally, this node was used to manage portals how they used to be implemented in a prototype version of The Story Machine, but portals were later implemented in the engine itself. This node used to be capable of switching [Viewport]s of children without ever leaving the tree. This behaviour was very buggy. With the new portal implementation, child nodes simply use the parent [Viewport] of the [SubWorld] instead.
[b]Note:[/b] This node means that [method Viewport.find_world_3d] from [method Node.get_viewport] may no longer return the actual [World3D] of the node. Use [method Node3D.get_world_3d] in order to obtain the correct [World3D].

method.name: find_world_3d
method.description: Returns the [World3D] the [SubWorld] is bound to. This may not be equal to [member world_3d] if it is undefined.

members.member: The [World3D] to bind to. If this is not defined, the [World3D] from the parent [Viewport] in the tree will be taken instead.

member.name: force_viewport
member.deprecated: Used in the old implementation. This will no longer have any effect.

members.member: The [Viewport] to force the [SubWorld] to use. The given [Viewport] must use the same world as [member world_3d], if it is defined. If [member world_3d] is not defined, then any [Viewport] can be used and the [World3D] will be taken from it.

signal.name: viewport_changed
signal.deprecated: Used in the old implementation. This will no longer be emitted by the node.
signal.description: Emitted when the main [Viewport] of the [SubWorld] is changed.
